item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Retail investors sold -$250 million worth of technology ETFs last week, their largest wee...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Retail investors sold -$250 million worth of technology ETFs last week, their largest weekly sale in at least 2 years.
This follows 4 consecutive weekly purchases, totaling +$1.2 billion.
Retail investors have sold technology ETFs in 9 of the last 20 weeks, a frequency not seen in at least 2 years.
Overall, retail purchases of equity ETFs fell to +$2.5 billion last week, near the lowest level since late 2023.
By comparison, retail's weekly purchases averaged +$8.0 billion in the first few weeks of 2026.
Many retail investors were shaken out last week.

item.title: @Hedgeye: A lot of what's on the Hedgeye short list used to be on the long list. That's not a contradiction....
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
A lot of what's on the Hedgeye short list used to be on the long list.
That's not a contradiction. That's the process.
We get long when the Signal says the phase is bullish. That phase might last six months. It might last six years. Nobody knows in advance, so nobody pretends to.
When TRADE and TREND break, the position changes sides. Same ticker, different phase.
It works the other way too. A name below its TRADE line gets sold on the rips. If it proves it can get back above that line, it gets bought on the dips.
None of that requires an opinion on the company, the CEO or the headline. It requires a Signal and the discipline to follow it.
These are just tickers. Not a marriage. Not a religion.

item.title: @WatcherGuru: JUST IN: Jensen Huang releases statement after being reinstated as Nvidia $NVDA CEO. "I am honoured...
item.dc:creator: @WatcherGuru
item.description:
JUST IN: Jensen Huang releases statement after being reinstated as Nvidia $NVDA CEO.
"I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.
I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.
I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period.
I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work."
item.content:encoded:

"I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution.

I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.

I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period.

I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work."

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Nvidia's board has listened. It has been a long 14 days, but we are pleased to see Nvidia's, $NVDA,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Nvidia's board has listened.
It has been a long 14 days, but we are pleased to see Nvidia's, $NVDA, board agree with our view to reinstate Jensen Huang.
From day one of this controversy, we maintained a firm view:
The door for Jensen Huang to return should never have been closed without a thorough and independent investigation.
Despite the board explicitly ruling out his return just days ago, we remained firm in this view.
This weekend, something clearly began to change behind the scenes, as we highlighted just 14 hours ago.
President Trump called for Jensen Huang's return, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the door was open, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.
Today, the leader of the AI Revolution is back.
Congratulations to all!

Despite the board explicitly ruling out his return just days ago, we remained firm in this view.

This weekend, something clearly began to change behind the scenes, as we highlighted just 14 hours ago.

President Trump called for Jensen Huang's return, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said the door was open, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work."

item.title: @wallstengine: JENSEN HUANG IS BACK AS NVIDIA CEO $NVDA announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Preside...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JENSEN HUANG IS BACK AS NVIDIA CEO
$NVDA announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President, CEO and a member of its board, effective immediately, following a unanimous board vote.
The decision reverses the board's earlier position against reinstating Huang.
Nvidia says the board held a series of discussions with Huang and received input from senior U.S. government officials before concluding that his return poses no national security risk.
Board Chair Harvey Jones will remain in his position, while Colette Kress will continue as CFO after serving as interim CEO.
The independent investigation into Huang's conduct and the reported foreign intelligence effort will continue, with Huang pledging full cooperation. Nvidia is also establishing additional compliance oversight and searching for a Chief Compliance Officer.
Huang said:
"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution."
"I can't wait to get back to work."

Applied Digital has signed an 18-year agreement with an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for 150 MW of AI data center capacity, generating $5.4B in contracted revenue.
The deal could grow to $12.7B over 33 years if all renewal options are exercised, with capacity delivery expected to begin in H1 2028.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 198...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 1980s.
Net equity inflows measure foreign purchases of US stocks minus US investors' purchases of foreign equities.
This figure has risen nearly +5.0 percentage points since the 2022 bear market low.
Meanwhile, net debt inflows, which measure foreign purchases of US debt securities, such as Treasuries minus US purchases of foreign debt securities, are down to ~1.8%, their lowest since 2022.
As a result, net equity inflows have surpassed net debt inflows as a % of GDP by the widest margin since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
In other words, foreign investors are increasingly directing money towards US equities rather than US bonds.
Overseas demand for US equities has never been this strong.

item.title: @wallstengine: JPMorgan says $TSLA's new FSD v15 raises the bar for rivals, calling it "another illustration of Te...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JPMorgan says $TSLA's new FSD v15 raises the bar for rivals, calling it "another illustration of Tesla's head start in consumer autonomy."
Tesla began rolling out FSD (Supervised) v15 to its first customers over the weekend, with broader availability expected in December.
The update introduces a significantly revised driving architecture, including an upgraded vision system shared across FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus, new Tesla Reality View visualizations, and navigation capabilities learned from fleet data.
Tesla claims the update delivers a roughly 25x improvement in handling safety-critical driving scenarios, alongside better environmental perception and driving behavior.
JPMorgan also highlights improved computing efficiency, which could reduce the need for near-term upgrades to Tesla's next-generation AI5 hardware, potentially limiting upgrade challenges to older pre-HW4 vehicles, which it estimates account for roughly 40% of Tesla's fleet.
The firm says the release comes as Rivian prepares to unveil its autonomy roadmap on December 9, Ford targets a 2027 launch, and GM works toward eyes-off highway driving in 2028.
JPMorgan maintains its Neutral rating on Tesla.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Once again, something appears to be happening behind the scenes. President Trump just explicitly ca...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Once again, something appears to be happening behind the scenes.
President Trump just explicitly called on Nvidia's, $NVDA, board to rehire Jensen Huang.
On top of this, he said Jensen returning would be "the best thing for the USA."
Just 10 days ago, Trump was calling for Tim Cook to replace Jensen Huang.
Hours ago, Treasury Secretary Bessent reversed his previous demand that Nvidia hire an "outside CEO."
When asked whether Jensen Huang could return, Bessent responded, "Jensen is on the outside now," acknowledging that he could return.
Attorney General Todd Blanche has also questioned the allegations surrounding Huang's departure, saying he has "certainly" not concluded that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.
In a matter of days, the Trump Admin's public position has shifted from calling for Jensen Huang's replacement to openly supporting his reinstatement.
The Trump Administration and Nvidia's shareholders appear to be aligned.
Pressure on Nvidia's board is mounting.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US businesses are forming at an unprecedented rate:
There were 501,609 US new business applications in October.
This marks the 7th consecutive month with business formation above 500,000.
This is also more than double the 235,730 recorded in April 2020, during the pandemic.
Since January 2025, new business applications have averaged 495,666 per month.
By comparison, the 2018-2019 pre-pandemic average stood at 292,344, or 41% lower.
The rapid adoption of AI is making it easier and cheaper to launch new businesses.
US entrepreneurial activity is skyrocketing.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The bears are having their moment. After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The bears are having their moment.
After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last 4 years, the bears finally got their moment last week.
However, in 3 to 6 months, we are going to look back at this correction and realize it was just that: a correction.
There is a widespread narrative right now that Nvidia, $NVDA, is quite literally going to collapse. This is a stock that was trading at a record high on October 6th, worth nearly $6 trillion, and the inventor of the most advanced chips in the world (it's not even close).
That's how deeply pessimistic sentiment has become over the last seven weeks.
Even if Nvidia produced half as much revenue as they are guiding for their next fiscal year, this company would still produce close to $400 billion in annual revenue.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted three consecutive quarters with earnings growth above 25% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth.
And, sentiment flipped so quickly that the S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average on Friday. Not even 2020 and 2008 saw such an occurrence.
The reality is that AI truly is the "next big thing" and the AI buildout is only accelerating.
Bears will sound smart, bulls will make money.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The median US home-sale price fell -0.4% YoY in October, to $388,634, posting its first Y...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The median US home-sale price fell -0.4% YoY in October, to $388,634, posting its first YoY decline since May 2023.
This marks a sharp reversal from the +2.5% YoY increase in August.
To put this into perspective, home sales prices have increased in nearly every month since 2013, except for a brief period in 2023.
The largest YoY increase over this period was recorded in May 2021, at +24.3%.
The recent decline comes as the total number of homes for sale rose +0.9% MoM in October, to 1,526,984, the largest total since early 2020, as housing demand weakened.
US housing is cooling off.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The Nvidia situation is evolving. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has completely changed his vi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The Nvidia situation is evolving.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has completely changed his view on Nvidia, $NVDA, over the last 7 days.
Last Sunday, Bessent called for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia and said its board needed to hire a new CEO from “outside” the company.
Today, when asked about Jensen Huang returning as CEO, Bessent said:
“Well, Jensen is on the outside now.”
When pressed on whether Jensen Huang should return, Bessent said, “I think we have to see where the buck stops,” clearly leaving the door open.
This comes just 2 days after President Trump publicly said Jensen Huang should “apologize and return.”
Something is happening behind the scenes.

This would also mark gold's largest 3-month rolling price decline since 1981.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold's biggest 3-month drawdown was -22.2%.
Meanwhile, silver prices are down -38.7% since the start of September, putting them on track for their biggest 3-month rolling decline since 2008, when prices fell -45.3%.
By comparison, silver's largest 3-month rolling decline on record was -63.6% in 1980.
Gold and silver are experiencing historic selling pressure.

History says last week's volatility will soon be met by dip buyers.
The Volatility Index, $VIX, jumped +16.6 points this week, to 35.9 points, its highest weekly close since April 2025.
This marks its 5th-largest weekly increase on record.
Following the 4 weekly VIX spikes of at least 16.5 points since 1990, the S&P 500 rallied +5.1% on average over the next trading day.
The index also gained +3.3% over the following week, on average, with positive returns in all 4 historical occurrences.
Over the next 3 months, the S&P 500 returned +5.9% on average.
In the most recent occurrence, following the post-Liberation Day VIX spike in April 2025, the index rallied +22.7% over the next 3 months.
History suggests the market is set for a relief rally.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US technology ETFs are seeing massive wave of deleveraging:
The 3x leveraged long Semiconductor ETF, $SOXL, is down -90% from its June peak, to its lowest since September 2025.
This marks its 2nd-largest drawdown since the fund's inception in March 2010, surpassed only by the -91% decline during the 2022 bear market.
By comparison, the fund dropped -89% during the July 2024-April 2025 period.
Meanwhile, the 3x leveraged long Nasdaq 100 ETF, $TQQQ, is down -53% from its June peak to its lowest since early April.
Since October 5th alone, the fund has dropped -51%.
For perspective, $TQQQ fell -61% during the February-April 2025 drawdown.
Leveraged tech funds have experienced a historic liquidation wave.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US equity market experienced just one of its sharpest sell-offs on record:
The S&P 500 fell -11.6% from its October 6th peak in just 33 trading days, placing the decline among the 15 fastest corrections since 1928.
By comparison, at the start of the 2022 bear market, it took 34 sessions for the index to fall at least -10%.
During the 2020 pandemic selloff, the same decline took just 6 trading days, while in March 2025 it took 17 sessions.
Overall, 4 of the 15 fastest corrections since 1928 have occurred over the last 6 years.
Meanwhile, 94% of S&P 500 stocks were down last week, with 111 declining by at least -10%.
At the same time, 11 stocks in the index were down by at least -20%.
Market sentiment has become extremely pessimistic.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The 10Y Note yield has traded above 5.00% for 27 trading days so far in 2026, the longest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The 10Y Note yield has traded above 5.00% for 27 trading days so far in 2026, the longest streak for any year since 2007.
Last week, the 10Y Note yield surged +29 basis points, moving back above 5.00% and marking its largest weekly increase since April 2025.
The 10Y is now on track for its longest period above 5.00% since 2006, when 65 trading days above this threshold were recorded.
Year-to-date, the 10Y Note yield is up +94 basis points, to 5.10%, after peaking at 5.36% in early October, its highest level since 2002.
This puts the yield on track for its 6th consecutive annual increase.
Higher for longer has become the new normal.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China's economic slowdown is deepening: China's retail sales rose just +0.4% YoY in October, the 3r...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China's economic slowdown is deepening:
China's retail sales rose just +0.4% YoY in October, the 3rd-lowest reading since December 2022, and well below the expected +0.8% growth.
This marks a sharp deceleration from a +1.1% YoY increase in September.
Retail sales are now on pace to end the year with their weakest growth since 2020.
Meanwhile, industrial production grew +4.8% YoY last month, down from +5.5% in September, and the slowest expansion in 3 months.
Furthermore, fixed-asset investment fell -8.1% YoY in the first 10 months of 2026, its biggest decline since the 2020 pandemic.
In October alone, investment dropped -16.9% YoY, the largest decline on record outside the pandemic.
China's domestic demand continues to deteriorate.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: What's happening with sentiment? It's hard to remember a time with as much negativity as we are see...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
What's happening with sentiment?
It's hard to remember a time with as much negativity as we are seeing now.
The world is in its biggest technological revolution in history, yet so many people want it to fail. Why?
AI has the potential to create a world of unprecedented abundance, and this should be a time for optimism.
Instead of focusing on the opportunities ahead, the conversation is dominated by fear, skepticism, and predictions of collapse.
Once again, the comments on this post will prove our point exactly.
Every major technological revolution in history has been met with skepticism, but progress has continued regardless.
The opportunities being created right now are generational.
Don't let short-term market sentiment blind you to long-term opportunity.

AI has the potential to create a world of unprecedented abundance, and this should be a time for optimism.

Instead of focusing on the opportunities ahead, the conversation is dominated by fear, skepticism, and predictions of collapse.

Once again, the comments on this post will prove our point exactly.

Every major technological revolution in history has been met with skepticism, but progress has continued regardless.

The opportunities being created right now are generational.

Don't let short-term market sentiment blind you to long-term opportunity.

US stocks have rarely been this oversold:
The S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, its widest deviation since August 2015.
This also marks its 3rd-largest deviation in at least 20 years.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index’s largest deviation from its 50-DMA was 3.6 standard deviations.
Not even the 2020 Pandemic crash saw such extreme oversold conditions, with the S&P 500 falling 3.8 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average in February.
During the 2022 bear market and the April 2025 post-"Liberation Day" selloff, the S&P 500 fell 3.2 and 3.3 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, respectively.
This has been one of the sharpest market sell-offs in history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Inflation in Japan is accelerating: Japan's CPI inflation excluding fresh food jumped +2.1% YoY in...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Inflation in Japan is accelerating:
Japan's CPI inflation excluding fresh food jumped +2.1% YoY in September, its highest YoY increase since December 2025.
Since May, Japan's CPI inflation has risen +0.6 percentage points.
Furthermore, CPI excluding fresh food and energy surged +2.4% YoY, its largest YoY increase since January.
Overall CPI inflation rose +2.1% YoY last month, its highest reading since November 2025.
This comes as the Iran War continues to fuel inflationary pressures in Japan, which relies heavily on imported food and energy.
Meanwhile, Japan's major food and beverage companies planned price increases for 3,153 items in October, the 2nd consecutive monthly reading above 3,000 for the first time since July 2023.
Inflationary pressures in Japan are broadening again.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: This past week's -10.4% drop in the Nasdaq 100 was one of the rarest weekly declines in 4...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: This past week's -10.4% drop in the Nasdaq 100 was one of the rarest weekly declines in 40 years.
Of the last 2,133 trading weeks, just 11 saw declines of this magnitude or worse.
That's 0.52% of all weeks, a 3.27 standard deviation move based on the historical mean and volatility.
Of course, market returns exhibit "fat tails," meaning extreme moves occur more frequently than a normal distribution would predict.
However, even accounting for the fact that extreme market moves are more common than traditional statistical models suggest, this was a historically rare selloff.
Volatility returns when markets least expect it.

Crypto has now seen $2.3 billion in levered positions liquidated in 24 hours, the 13th largest liquidation event in history.

All crypto gains since President Trump won the 2024 Election are gone, a total of -$2.3 trillion.

Liquidity crunches like these are when 24/7 markets can be dangerous.

As outlined in our Article below, liquidity must be restored for markets to bottom.

item.description:
Investor positioning in copper is cratering:
Speculative investors sold -$1.3 billion in Comex copper futures in the week ending November 10th, marking the 7th consecutive weekly sale.
This group includes hedge funds, commodity trading advisers (CTAs), and other institutional investors.
Since September 22nd, they have sold a cumulative -$10.8 billion.
This brings long speculative investor positioning down to ~$5.2 billion, its lowest since October 2025.
Meanwhile, copper futures fell -5.3% on Wednesday, marking their largest daily decline since July 2026.
Copper prices are now down -18.2% from their September peak, to $5.67 per pound, their lowest level since April.
The copper market is seeing a massive shift in sentiment.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The semiconductor trade is still popular among fund managers: 39% of global fund managers said "lon...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The semiconductor trade is still popular among fund managers:
39% of global fund managers said "long global semiconductors" was the most crowded trade, according to a BofA survey of 169 fund managers overseeing $461 billion in assets conducted between November 6th and November 12th.
This marks the 6th consecutive month that semiconductors have held the top spot.
However, this figure is down from the 82% peak recorded in July this year.
Meanwhile, “Short China Stocks” ranked 2nd for the first time, with 14% of respondents identifying it as the most crowded trade.
By comparison, "Long Magnificent 7" and "Short Treasuries" were considered the most crowded trades just by 12% and 10% of fund managers, respectively.
Investor appetite for semiconductor stocks remains strong.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The 3-month correlation between the S&P 500 and gold is up to +0.35, doubling since Febru...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The 3-month correlation between the S&P 500 and gold is up to +0.35, doubling since February.
The correlation between these two assets has remained positive throughout the year, unlike in 2025, when it was negative for most months.
Since the Iran War began, gold has increasingly traded like a risky asset rather than a hedge against market declines, moving alongside equities.
Year-to-date, gold prices are now down -17%, on track for their biggest annual decline since 2013.
This comes as elevated energy prices, resurging inflation, and rising interest rates have heavily weighed on gold.
Furthermore, recent equity market losses have forced some investors to liquidate gold holdings to offset losses elsewhere.
Gold is caught up in the liquidity crunch.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US Pending Homes Sales Index dropped -4.7% MoM in October, to 63.0 points, its lowest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US Pending Homes Sales Index dropped -4.7% MoM in October, to 63.0 points, its lowest level on record in data going back to 2001.
All regions posted declines, with the West seeing the steepest drop, at -6.9%, while sales in the South, the biggest home-selling region, fell -6.3%.
YoY, sales plunged -16.7% in the biggest annual decline since August 2023.
Over the last 2 months, the Pending Homes Sales Index has fallen -8.2 points, its largest 2-month decline since October 2022.
US pending home sales are now -51% below their post-pandemic recovery peak.
The US housing market is coming to a halt.

item.dc:creator: @KeithMcCullough
item.description:
In a fractal system, volatility isn’t a constant. When the Volatility Regime shifts into the F-Bucket, the Fractal Dimension (Risk Range™ Signal) stops moving smoothly and starts jumping...
The Range expands and collapses at a faster rate, and each leg down feeds the next one through the feedback loop.
That’s the self-similar cascade, now running at a higher speed. Do NOT cover shorts below your MIN position SIZE

item.title: @Hedgeye: There are 11 sectors in the S&P 500. Most of the profession treats them as one ticker. Buy the inde...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
There are 11 sectors in the S&P 500.
Most of the profession treats them as one ticker. Buy the index, hold the index, hope the index.
We call that being a SPY Monkey.
The S&P can be bearish on TRADE and TREND while a handful of its sectors are working. The job is to own what the Signal says is working and avoid or short what it says isn't. That's active management. It's a better business, too.
Then count the score honestly. One week tells you almost nothing. Look at one month. Look at three. TREND is three months or more for a reason.
Every game has a winner and a loser. So does every cycle.
To learn how we map sectors to the Quads, start at https://app.hedgeye.com/education

item.title: @wallstengine: NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS $NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, re...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS
$NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, replacing Puma as the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier starting in the 2027 season.
The deal will see Nike produce uniforms for F1 staff, along with F1-branded shoes, clothing and accessories for fans. Nike will also supply apparel for F1 Academy, the racing series focused on developing female drivers.
The partnership kicks off today, November 20, with a limited-edition Nike x Las Vegas Grand Prix collection available at select locations in Las Vegas.
Nike's last major involvement in Formula 1 was through its footwear partnership with seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher, which ended in 2002.
item.content:encoded:
NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS

$NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, replacing Puma as the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier starting in the 2027 season.

The deal will see Nike produce uniforms for F1 staff, along with F1-branded shoes, clothing and accessories for fans. Nike will also supply apparel for F1 Academy, the racing series focused on developing female drivers.

The partnership kicks off today, November 20, with a limited-edition Nike x Las Vegas Grand Prix collection available at select locations in Las Vegas.

Nike's last major involvement in Formula 1 was through its footwear partnership with seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher, which ended in 2002.

item.title: @wallstengine: Citigroup $C underestimated its risk-weighted assets by about $35B after incorrectly recording trad...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Citigroup $C underestimated its risk-weighted assets by about $35B after incorrectly recording trades at its UK securities unit.
The bank used an internal risk model that regulators hadn't approved for those transactions. When the trades were recalculated using the correct model, the amount of assets used to determine Citi's required capital reserves jumped by roughly $35B.
Citi says it identified and fixed the issue this summer and injected additional capital into its European subsidiary to restore its financial buffers.
The bank says the subsidiary remained above regulatory minimum capital requirements throughout.

Citi says it identified and fixed the issue this summer and injected additional capital into its European subsidiary to restore its financial buffers.

The bank says the subsidiary remained above regulatory minimum capital requirements throughout.

item.title: @wallstengine: HSBC upgrades $TSLA from Reduce to Hold and raises its price target to $359 from $157, citing a pot...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HSBC upgrades $TSLA from Reduce to Hold and raises its price target to $359 from $157, citing a potential acquisition by SpaceX.
The bank now values Tesla using two scenarios:
SpaceX acquisition: $507/share.
Standalone valuation: $212/share, up from $193, based on Tesla's underlying businesses.
HSBC assigns a 50% weighting to each scenario, resulting in its new $359 target.
"Given the acquisition newsflow, we believe the current share price of Tesla offers an anchor, irrespective of the fundamentals."
However, HSBC acknowledges there is no guarantee a deal will happen or receive shareholder approval, and that Tesla could trade on its fundamentals alone if an acquisition does not materialize.

item.title: @wallstengine: CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT China's sovereign wealth fund, Chin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT
China's sovereign wealth fund, China Investment Corporation, is negotiating terms with private equity firms that would allow Chinese investors to recover their money if U.S. or European sanctions are imposed, without forcing funds to sell their assets.
Proposals include repayment arrangements tied to fund exits, separate investment vehicles and provisions allowing investors to opt out of individual deals.
Chinese state-backed investors stopped making new U.S. private equity commitments during last year's trade war, after previously backing firms including Blackstone, Carlyle, Thoma Bravo and Vista Equity.
Fund advisers say Trump's recent China visit helped revive CIC's interest, although no new investment commitments have been announced.
item.content:encoded:
CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT

China's sovereign wealth fund, China Investment Corporation, is negotiating terms with private equity firms that would allow Chinese investors to recover their money if U.S. or European sanctions are imposed, without forcing funds to sell their assets.

Proposals include repayment arrangements tied to fund exits, separate investment vehicles and provisions allowing investors to opt out of individual deals.

Chinese state-backed investors stopped making new U.S. private equity commitments during last year's trade war, after previously backing firms including Blackstone, Carlyle, Thoma Bravo and Vista Equity.

Fund advisers say Trump's recent China visit helped revive CIC's interest, although no new investment commitments have been announced.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's clear now more than ever: Ultimately, this bear market in tech stocks will be remembered as th...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's clear now more than ever:
Ultimately, this bear market in tech stocks will be remembered as the best buying opportunity of the last decade.
Unless your view is that the AI is worthless and the AI Revolution is over, many key parts of this market are extremely cheap.
Democrats will be more friendly to AI than expected, Nvidia will survive its leadership crisis, and concerns around CapEx and free cash flow will prove to be overblown.
To top it off, current sentiment is as if the market has just gone through another 2008, all while the S&P 500 is posting +32% earnings growth.
The comments on this post will show you just how polarized sentiment has become in the direction "bubble" callers.
Fear creates an investor's biggest opportunity.
Bookmark this post.

Ultimately, this bear market in tech stocks will be remembered as the best buying opportunity of the last decade.

Unless your view is that the AI is worthless and the AI Revolution is over, many key parts of this market are extremely cheap.

Democrats will be more friendly to AI than expected, Nvidia will survive its leadership crisis, and concerns around CapEx and free cash flow will prove to be overblown.

To top it off, current sentiment is as if the market has just gone through another 2008, all while the S&P 500 is posting +32% earnings growth.

The comments on this post will show you just how polarized sentiment has become in the direction "bubble" callers.

Fear creates an investor's biggest opportunity.

Bookmark this post.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for more than $500M, plus potential emp...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for more than $500M, plus potential employee earnouts, The Information reports.
Inception develops diffusion-based language models designed to generate responses faster than traditional AI models like those powering ChatGPT and Claude.
Nvidia plans to use Inception's technology and researchers to strengthen its Nemotron open-weight models and AI systems for robotics.
All three co-founders are expected to join Nvidia. Microsoft had also expressed interest in a similar deal before Nvidia's talks advanced.

item.title: @wallstengine: WHITE HOUSE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS RESIGNS - AXIOS Cairncross leads the Office of...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
WHITE HOUSE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS RESIGNS - AXIOS
Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. The job requires Senate confirmation.
He did not want to serve another two years, and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation of a successor before Democrats take control of the Senate in January, according to two sources. Axios describes the departure as amicable.
His head of policy and senior adviser, Thomas Lind, left in June and joined OpenAI in October.
On Monday, Cairncross told Semafor that a cyberattack was not behind the nationwide air traffic ground stop and other outages, blaming upgrades to old technology.
The White House has not yet responded to Axios' request for comment.
item.content:encoded:
WHITE HOUSE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS RESIGNS - AXIOS

Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. The job requires Senate confirmation.

He did not want to serve another two years, and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation of a successor before Democrats take control of the Senate in January, according to two sources. Axios describes the departure as amicable.

His head of policy and senior adviser, Thomas Lind, left in June and joined OpenAI in October.

On Monday, Cairncross told Semafor that a cyberattack was not behind the nationwide air traffic ground stop and other outages, blaming upgrades to old technology.

The White House has not yet responded to Axios' request for comment.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE
New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:
- Control apps and navigate devices - Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code - Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services - Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents
Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.
Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.
item.content:encoded:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE

New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:

- Control apps and navigate devices
- Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code
- Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services
- Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents

Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.

Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS Nvidia and Microsoft...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS
Nvidia and Microsoft $MSFT announced several new AI infrastructure and software integrations at Microsoft Ignite, covering cloud computing, enterprise AI models, robotics and local AI.
Here are the key developments:
Vera Rubin on Azure: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are already running in Microsoft's data centers, with Azure expanding access to Rubin-powered infrastructure for AI training, reasoning and inference.
Enterprise AI models: Microsoft Foundry is expanding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 open models, allowing companies to customize AI models using their own data and deploy them through Microsoft's cloud services.
55% accuracy improvement, 15x lower cost: EY used Nvidia Nemotron through Microsoft Foundry to improve the accuracy of corporate purchasing-record classification by 55% while reducing costs by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models in its evaluation.
AI on local servers and PCs: Azure Local is adding support for Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and Jetson platforms for industrial AI and robotics. The companies are also demonstrating AI models running directly on Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark.
Microsoft's own AI development: Microsoft AI is using Nvidia Dynamo software to accelerate inference during model post-training, while Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs are being used for Bing search models.
The companies are also expanding confidential computing to protect sensitive enterprise models and data during processing on Vera Rubin infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
$NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS

Nvidia and Microsoft $MSFT announced several new AI infrastructure and software integrations at Microsoft Ignite, covering cloud computing, enterprise AI models, robotics and local AI.

Here are the key developments:

Vera Rubin on Azure: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are already running in Microsoft's data centers, with Azure expanding access to Rubin-powered infrastructure for AI training, reasoning and inference.

Enterprise AI models: Microsoft Foundry is expanding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 open models, allowing companies to customize AI models using their own data and deploy them through Microsoft's cloud services.

55% accuracy improvement, 15x lower cost: EY used Nvidia Nemotron through Microsoft Foundry to improve the accuracy of corporate purchasing-record classification by 55% while reducing costs by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models in its evaluation.

AI on local servers and PCs: Azure Local is adding support for Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and Jetson platforms for industrial AI and robotics. The companies are also demonstrating AI models running directly on Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark.

Microsoft's own AI development: Microsoft AI is using Nvidia Dynamo software to accelerate inference during model post-training, while Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs are being used for Bing search models.

The companies are also expanding confidential computing to protect sensitive enterprise models and data during processing on Vera Rubin infrastructure.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META PLANS $300 MUSE CHARM WITH FREE VERIZON 5G, TARGETS 10M WEARABLE DEVICE SALES IN H2 2026 Meta...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META PLANS $300 MUSE CHARM WITH FREE VERIZON 5G, TARGETS 10M WEARABLE DEVICE SALES IN H2 2026
Meta plans to price its pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device at $300, with up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G service to access its Muse AI assistant.
The company has delayed its smartwatch launch to 2027 to prioritize Charm, using technology originally developed for the watch.
Meta has also set an internal target of selling 10 million wearable devices in the second half of 2026 and reaching nearly 7 million monthly active wearable users by year-end.
For context, EssilorLuxottica reported selling more than 7 million pairs of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses in 2025.
Sorce: The Information

item.title: @wallstengine: NETFLIX, AMAZON, YOUTUBE & FOX EXPECTED TO BID FOR 2030 FIFA WORLD CUP U.S. MEDIA RIGHTS First-roun...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NETFLIX, AMAZON, YOUTUBE & FOX EXPECTED TO BID FOR 2030 FIFA WORLD CUP U.S. MEDIA RIGHTS
First-round bids are due today, with media executives expecting the winning offer to reach around $1.5 billion or more, CNBC reports.
Disney/ESPN is out after deciding it couldn't justify the price, even with a partner. Apple and Skydance also won't bid, while NBCUniversal/Telemundo remains undecided.
FIFA prefers to sell English and Spanish rights together and plans to select a winner by year-end.
A streaming winner would not be required to make any games available on free TV.
Source: CNBC
item.content:encoded:
NETFLIX, AMAZON, YOUTUBE & FOX EXPECTED TO BID FOR 2030 FIFA WORLD CUP U.S. MEDIA RIGHTS

First-round bids are due today, with media executives expecting the winning offer to reach around $1.5 billion or more, CNBC reports.

Disney/ESPN is out after deciding it couldn't justify the price, even with a partner. Apple and Skydance also won't bid, while NBCUniversal/Telemundo remains undecided.

FIFA prefers to sell English and Spanish rights together and plans to select a winner by year-end.

A streaming winner would not be required to make any games available on free TV.

Source: CNBC

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia VP Ian Buck on CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO: "I don't know any other CFO that ca...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia VP Ian Buck on CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO:
"I don't know any other CFO that can speak to how many tokens per second Vera Rubin and NVL72 can deliver on a model like Nemotron or Meta Muse, and understand what it means."
"I mean, she intimately understands that."
"She understands not only our business but the whole ecosystem of people that are supplying compute."
Buck also said members of Kress's team are embedded throughout Nvidia's product departments, highlighting how closely her finance organization works with the company's engineering and product teams.
Source: Yahoo Finance

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic just pulled off the biggest IPO in history. Here's who made billions and millions of dollars:
THE EMPLOYEES 600 employees with stakes worth $100M+ 2,800 employees with stakes worth $10M+ 4,250 of its 5,300 employees estimated to become millionaires
THE BIG TWO Amazon: $193B stake (10.7x) Google: $177B stake (5.3x)
THE 7 CO-FOUNDERS: ~$167B COMBINED
Each is worth roughly $24B and sold about $280M in shares through the IPO.
Dario Amodei Daniela Amodei Tom Brown Jack Clark Jared Kaplan Sam McCandlish Chris Olah
Jack Clark could become the UK's richest person.
THE EARLY INVESTORS
Lightspeed Venture Partners: ~$30B ICONIQ Capital: ~$30B Jaan Tallinn, Skype co-founder: ~$19B Eric Schmidt, former Google CEO: ~$18B Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures: Stake worth billions SK Telecom: ~$3B windfall
Coatue Management: Invested ~$4.75B Singapore's GIC: Invested ~$4.5B Dustin Moskovitz, Facebook co-founder: Among Anthropic's earliest investors
WALL STREET
Goldman Sachs: ~$113M in underwriting fees Morgan Stanley: ~$113M in underwriting fees Entire 22-bank syndicate: ~$550M in fees
All stake values are approximate, based on $100 per share.

Entire 22-bank syndicate: ~$550M in fees

All stake values are approximate, based on $100 per share.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: AMD, $AMD, officially denies claims made by Hunterbrook Media that sent the stock -13% lo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: AMD, $AMD, officially denies claims made by Hunterbrook Media that sent the stock -13% lower, saying that the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," per Bloomberg.
"AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," a spokesperson said.
"We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity," they added.
Hunterbrook Capital released the report with a short position in the stock.

"We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity," they added.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Volatility tells you which game you're playing. $VIX below 19, investable. Above 19, the Chop bucke...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Volatility tells you which game you're playing.
$VIX below 19, investable.
Above 19, the Chop bucket. The bottom of the range starts falling out. Lower lows, big lower highs, and the selling picks up pace.
Volatility in the 30s, the F*ck bucket. Ranges widen and moves get violent.
Know your bucket before you size your position. #Process
item.content:encoded:

item.title: @wallstengine: HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERV...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERVER MAKER
Hunterbrook's new investigation into AMD found that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2025, continued posting server software updates containing newer AMD firmware after the restrictions took effect.
Key findings:
• Firmware updates: IEIT posted at least six server BIOS updates containing newer versions of AMD's firmware after being blacklisted, including an update posted October 19, 2026.
• Linked companies: Hunterbrook found that three other server vendors, Aivres, Kaytus and Maginfra, published firmware files that were 99.94% identical to IEIT's. Kaytus identifies IEIT as its ultimate parent.
• AI chips: AMD's own website lists Aivres as a partner offering servers powered by its Instinct AI accelerators, including the MI300X and MI325X.
• China revenue: AMD generated $7.75B, or 22.4% of its 2025 revenue, from customers billed in China and Hong Kong.
• Supply chain: Two Chinese joint ventures controlled by Tongfu Microelectronics perform most of AMD's chip assembly, testing and packaging. AMD purchased roughly $2B in services from them in 2025.
AMD did not answer Hunterbrook's questions about whether it held export licenses for the companies involved.
The investigation does not establish that AMD violated export laws or determine how IEIT obtained the firmware.
Hunterbrook Capital disclosed that it was short $AMD at the time of publication.
item.content:encoded:
HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERVER MAKER

Hunterbrook's new investigation into AMD found that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2025, continued posting server software updates containing newer AMD firmware after the restrictions took effect.

Key findings:

• Firmware updates: IEIT posted at least six server BIOS updates containing newer versions of AMD's firmware after being blacklisted, including an update posted October 19, 2026.

• Linked companies: Hunterbrook found that three other server vendors, Aivres, Kaytus and Maginfra, published firmware files that were 99.94% identical to IEIT's. Kaytus identifies IEIT as its ultimate parent.

• AI chips: AMD's own website lists Aivres as a partner offering servers powered by its Instinct AI accelerators, including the MI300X and MI325X.

• China revenue: AMD generated $7.75B, or 22.4% of its 2025 revenue, from customers billed in China and Hong Kong.

• Supply chain: Two Chinese joint ventures controlled by Tongfu Microelectronics perform most of AMD's chip assembly, testing and packaging. AMD purchased roughly $2B in services from them in 2025.

AMD did not answer Hunterbrook's questions about whether it held export licenses for the companies involved.

The investigation does not establish that AMD violated export laws or determine how IEIT obtained the firmware.

Hunterbrook Capital disclosed that it was short $AMD at the time of publication.

item.title: @wallstengine: Anthropic rings the opening bell at Nasdaq following its record $81.3B IPO, which drew demand for n...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic rings the opening bell at Nasdaq following its record $81.3B IPO, which drew demand for nearly 7x the shares offered.
Here's who got shares:
Retail: About 15% of the IPO.
Institutions: Most received no shares as existing backers were prioritized, per Bloomberg.
Japan: Investors received about $3B, at the low end of the planned $3B to $3.5B allocation.
UK Retail: Over 100,000 UK investors participated, with nearly two-thirds receiving their full allocation.
Private placements: A separate $26B investment from seven tech companies at the $83 IPO price:
Google: $10B Nvidia: $10B AMD: $2.5B Broadcom: $1B Micron: $1B Microsoft: $1B TSMC: $500M
The private placement is separate from the $81.3B public offering, with investors receiving non-voting shares.

Anthropic rings the opening bell at Nasdaq following its record $81.3B IPO, which drew demand for nearly 7x the shares offered.

Japan: Investors received about $3B, at the low end of the planned $3B to $3.5B allocation.

UK Retail: Over 100,000 UK investors participated, with nearly two-thirds receiving their full allocation.

Private placements: A separate $26B investment from seven tech companies at the $83 IPO price:

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -3.2 million barrels last week, to 276.4 milli...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -3.2 million barrels last week, to 276.4 million barrels, its lowest level since August 1982.
This follows declines of -2.65 million barrels and -399,000 barrels in the previous two weeks.
Since the March high, US SPR inventories have collapsed -139.1 million barrels, or -34%, down in 33 of the last 34 weeks.
The SPR now stands -450.3 million barrels, or -62%, below its all-time high set in 2010.
This is also just 5.9 million barrels above its lowest level on record, set in the week ending August 20th, 1982.
US oil reserves have rarely been this low.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The S&P 500 has recorded 25 trading days with daily losses of at least -1% so far in 2026. This inc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The S&P 500 has recorded 25 trading days with daily losses of at least -1% so far in 2026.
This includes 22 days with losses between -1% and -2%, 2 days between -2% and -3%, and 1 session with a decline of -3% or more.
7, or 28%, of these trading days occurred in October and November.
This compares with 29 such sessions in 2025 and 19 in 2024.
By comparison, during the 2022 bear market, the S&P 500 recorded 63 trading days with losses of at least -1%.
For perspective, the average year since 1928 has seen 29 such days.
Market volatility is still in-line with the historical average.

item.title: @wallstengine: $500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ
In August, $NVDA announced a partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B to help customers like OpenAI, Anthropic and smaller AI cloud companies finance chip purchases.
But the agreement was only a few-page memorandum of understanding. None of the firms was obligated to raise any money, and no capital has been deployed.
Jensen Huang had initially pushed for an even larger $1T financing program, partly to support Nvidia's valuation as its earnings grew but its valuation multiple declined.
He accelerated the effort after Apollo and Blackstone helped rival Broadcom arrange $35B in chip financing for Anthropic.
The biggest obstacle has been Nvidia's willingness to guarantee the loans:
Nvidia was willing to provide credit support covering up to 25% of project costs.
Broadcom provided residual-value guarantees covering about 85% of Anthropic's $35B Project Big Sky and just under 75% of its $63B Project North Star.
As lenders have become more cautious about AI financing, they have pushed Nvidia to offer greater protection.
Nvidia has also been pulling back its financial guarantees. Earlier, reports of a proposed $250B Nvidia backstop for an OpenAI data center sent $NVDA shares down 5%, prompting Nvidia to cut its initial commitment in half.
Interim CEO Colette Kress has since signaled that future investments and guarantees will be evaluated more strictly.
Talks on the partnership's first chip-backed financing deal are still underway, but nothing is expected to close before 2027.
Apollo CEO Marc Rowan warned that without Nvidia providing financial guarantees, a large number of neocloud companies could lose access to capital.

item.title: @wallstengine: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on why the company offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees: The buyo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on why the company offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees:
The buyouts were meant to give employees a sense of agency in making their own career choices.
Microsoft isn't treating software engineers as obsolete. Software engineering will "thrive," but the way teams are organized and the work engineers do will change significantly with AI.
Employees will increasingly become managers of AI agents and systems that produce the work, with this shift expected across all jobs.
One Microsoft team of just 11 developers building Cowork now builds "a software factory that builds the product," rather than building the product directly.
As a 51-year-old incumbent, Microsoft isn't an AI-first company. The transition to AI-driven workflows will take longer than many expect, and some employees may choose to leave.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Japan's exports jumped +20.5% YoY in October, to a record $74 billion, the 2nd-largest mo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Japan's exports jumped +20.5% YoY in October, to a record $74 billion, the 2nd-largest monthly increase since October 2022.
Japan’s exports have now grown for 14 consecutive months, the longest streak since 2021-2023.
The surge was led by semiconductor manufacturing equipment shipments, which soared +49.7% YoY.
This was followed by electrical machinery exports, at +33.6% YoY growth, reflecting strong global investment in AI infrastructure.
Among regions, exports to Taiwan led with +42.7% YoY growth, followed by ASEAN at +34.7%, the US at +23.9%, the EU at +22.1%, and China at +13.3%.
Global chip demand is transforming the Japanese economy.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION Anthropic $ANT sold 980 mill...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION
Anthropic $ANT sold 980 million shares to raise $81.34 billion, up from the 825 million it originally planned and above its $70-$78 range.
About $79.4 billion goes to Anthropic. Existing shareholders selling 23.6 million shares get about $2 billion.
Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever, topping the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June before extra shares.
If underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares in their 30-day option, the raise would reach $93.5 billion, passing SpaceX's $85.7 billion total.
The price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted. With a $26 billion private placement from investors including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have more than $200 billion on its balance sheet, per the FT.
Shares start trading Thursday on Nasdaq.
item.content:encoded:
ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION

Anthropic $ANT sold 980 million shares to raise $81.34 billion, up from the 825 million it originally planned and above its $70-$78 range.

About $79.4 billion goes to Anthropic. Existing shareholders selling 23.6 million shares get about $2 billion.

Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever, topping the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June before extra shares.

If underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares in their 30-day option, the raise would reach $93.5 billion, passing SpaceX's $85.7 billion total.

The price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted. With a $26 billion private placement from investors including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have more than $200 billion on its balance sheet, per the FT.

Shares start trading Thursday on Nasdaq.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are rotating into defensive sectors at a historic pace: Consumer Staples, Healthcare, and...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are rotating into defensive sectors at a historic pace:
Consumer Staples, Healthcare, and Utilities have outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by +22.8 percentage points in October and November so far, on track for the largest 2-month rolling outperformance since 2001.
By comparison, the largest 2-month outperformance was recorded in 2000, at +40.9 percentage points.
Defensive sectors outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by +17.1 percentage points in October, their largest monthly outperformance since February 2001.
This follows a +5.8 percentage-point relative return so far in November.
Month-to-date, the Nasdaq 100 is down -4.9%, putting the index on track for its worst November since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
At the same time, Consumer Staples are up +2.9%, Healthcare is up +0.1%, while Utilities are down -0.3%.
Defensive sectors are showing a historic relative strength.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Elon Musk says Nvidia made a mistake removing Jensen Huang, confirms he's spoken with him privately and says he would hire him himself: "who wouldn't?"
"I would call Jensen, Michael Jordan, perhaps at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team."
"You got a winning streak that's just gonna happen, and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team. Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me."
"There's no one that can really replace Jensen. He does the roles of several people. He's managing supply chain. He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades. He understands his technology incredibly well."
"His team loves him. And many of them are there because of him, and have had higher offers to go elsewhere and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen."
"He's one of the most talented entrepreneur CEOs in history. Who wouldn't want to hire Jensen?"

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL LAUNCHES GEMINI 4 NEON
Google's new AI model is designed for complex coding, scientific research, analyzing docs and spreadsheets, and running AI agents that can complete multi-step tasks.
Beats Claude Opus 5.5 & GPT-6.2 Sol across several key benchmarks. Here's how they compare
(Neon / Opus 5.5 / GPT-6.2 Sol): AI Intelligence Index: 61 / 59 / 57 AutomationBench: 56.3% / 42.5% / 41.3% Advanced reasoning : 71.3% / 67.9% / 64.0% Science tasks: 70.5% / 63.3% / 68.0%
Neon ranks #3 overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, #1 on its Coding Agent Index, and #2 on the Vals Index and Agent Arena.
Google says Neon delivers a 32% lower cost per task than Gemini 4 Carbon at its default high thinking level.
Pricing: • Input: $3 per million tokens • Output: $15 per million tokens • Cached input: $0.15 per million tokens • Context window: 1 million tokens
It begins rolling out today through Gemini API, Google AI Studio and Gemini for business, as well as Google Antigravity and the Gemini app for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers.

item.description:
BREAKING: Anthropic, $ANT, has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, per Bloomberg.
The company is now expected to raise at least $68 billion through its IPO, plus another $26 billion in a private placement.
This brings the total offering to more than $94 billion, surpassing SpaceX’s record $86.2 billion IPO in June.
This marks the largest IPO in stock market history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global fund managers cut their technology exposure by -25 percentage points in early Nove...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global fund managers cut their technology exposure by -25 percentage points in early November, to a net 12%, their biggest monthly decline since June 2006.
This marks even a larger monthly decline than during the 2022 bear market or the 2008 Financial Crisis.
As a result, technology is no longer the most overweight sector among fund managers.
The largest overweight positions are currently in Pharmaceuticals, at 34%, and Industrials, at 19%.
A record 38% of surveyed institutional investors believe companies are overinvesting, up from ~20% in January.
At the same time, 52% expect Big Tech companies to announce CapEx reductions over the next 6 months, up from 30% in October.
Institutional investors are rotating out of technology stocks at a rapid pace.

item.title: @wallstengine: JPMORGAN IS TRYING TO SELL $2B OF QUALTRICS DEBT AT A 20% DISCOUNT JPMorgan is marketing bonds tied...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JPMORGAN IS TRYING TO SELL $2B OF QUALTRICS DEBT AT A 20% DISCOUNT
JPMorgan is marketing bonds tied to Qualtrics' $6.75B acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta at around 80 cents on the dollar, per FT.
The proposed terms: • Maturity: 6.5 years • Coupon: 8% • Issue price: 80 cents on the dollar • Implied yield: 12% to 13%
A group of banks, including JPMorgan, has been stuck holding more than $5B of acquisition debt since March after investors pulled back from software financing amid fears that AI could disrupt these businesses.
The banks had committed to providing the financing but couldn't sell the debt to outside investors, forcing them to fund the acquisition themselves.
JPMorgan is now trying to offload part of that debt before year-end, with the new bond sale expected to launch after Thanksgiving. Pricing is not yet final.
Qualtrics' existing term loan maturing in 2030 was also trading at around 82 cents on the dollar on Tuesday.
For comparison, cybersecurity firm Proofpoint just sold $2B of debt, including $1.25B in high-yield bonds that attracted more than $7B in orders and priced at an approximately 8.75% yield.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Why Nvidia Isn’t Going Up on Good Numbers 🔊 Nvidia ($NVDA) reported third-quarter revenue of $115....
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Why Nvidia Isn’t Going Up on Good Numbers
🔊
Nvidia ($NVDA) reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion after the bell yesterday. That’s more than double a year ago and above the $109.3 billion analysts expected.

item.description:
FED MINUTES FLAG RISKS IN THE AI BUILDOUT
Most Fed officials noted that AI-related debt has grown rapidly, much of it through "complex and opaque" financing structures.
Fed staff warned that circular financing arrangements and off-balance-sheet lease commitments among AI firms could amplify losses if AI investment returns disappoint.
Several officials warned that the AI investment surge could be excessive, potentially leading to lower-than-expected returns.
Many officials viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk, with demand straining supply and pushing up prices, including beyond the data center industry.

item.description:
More details, per FT:
Aschenbrenner has held talks with Jefferies about opening a prime brokerage account. The bank previously turned him away over concerns that his fund was not adequately hedged.
Situational Awareness is also working with Clear Street and is looking to hire a chief risk officer.
Aschenbrenner has also discussed raising additional capital from outside investors next year, although the plans remain preliminary.
During the summer crisis, the fund sold most of its public holdings to Citadel at a discount to repay lenders, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan. JPMorgan subsequently cut off lending.
The fund now has around 30 employees, compared with just eight disclosed in June.

item.title: @wallstengine: Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his he...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his hedge fund Situational Awareness nearly collapsed this summer.
The fund went from managing over $20B to needing an emergency rescue from Citadel within days after its AI bets went wrong.
It still manages over $10B, mostly in private investments, including a roughly $5B stake in Anthropic.
Despite pledging in July to stop borrowing, Aschenbrenner has discussed using leverage again and raising new capital. Neither plan is finalized.
Source: FT
item.content:encoded:
Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his hedge fund Situational Awareness nearly collapsed this summer.

The fund went from managing over $20B to needing an emergency rescue from Citadel within days after its AI bets went wrong.

It still manages over $10B, mostly in private investments, including a roughly $5B stake in Anthropic.

Despite pledging in July to stop borrowing, Aschenbrenner has discussed using leverage again and raising new capital. Neither plan is finalized.

Source: FT

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI REPORTS UP TO 14% PPA IMPROVEMENT ON $AMD GPU DESIGNS OpenAI says its AI models rewrote Syst...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI REPORTS UP TO 14% PPA IMPROVEMENT ON $AMD GPU DESIGNS
OpenAI says its AI models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL for AMD's already heavily optimized flagship GPU IP, delivering roughly a year's worth of chip-design progress in less than 5 months.
The improvements involve power, performance and area (PPA), with several results already moving into production:
GPU: Up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP.
Manufacturing: AMD has incorporated some AI-generated changes into a recent chip design sent for manufacturing, with others added to production design files for future versions.
CPU: AMD verified single-digit PPA improvements across key blocks of its upcoming next-generation flagship CPU.
OpenAI's Jalapeño chip: AI-assisted optimizations reduced standard-cell area by approximately 13% in its vector unit and 10% in its matrix unit, with the improvements verified on silicon.
OpenAI is also working with Synopsys to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model designed to use professional chip-design and verification tools.

item.title: @wallstengine: MICROSOFT TO USE $INTC'S EMIB PACKAGING FOR AZURE CHIPS $MSFT is the FIRST company to announce plan...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MICROSOFT TO USE $INTC'S EMIB PACKAGING FOR AZURE CHIPS
$MSFT is the FIRST company to announce plans to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for its own Azure silicon.
EMIB connects multiple chiplets within a single package, allowing more flexible chip designs.
The new long-term agreement with Intel also secures multi-year Xeon CPU supply for Azure, including next-gen Diamond Rapids processors.
The companies will also expand work on CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist acceleration and TDX confidential computing, including encryption of VM memory and CPU state during host migrations.
Intel says its existing Azure optimizations deliver:
- Up to 2.3x greater performance and memory flexibility in Azure M-series v4 VMs using Xeon 6 and CXL memory.
- Up to 2.5x faster SQL backups through QuickAssist-enabled Azure VMs.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Take a look at sentiment right now. Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are n...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Take a look at sentiment right now.
Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the "AI bubble has popped."
Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression.
In reality? The S&P 500 is up +7% YTD, +60% in 5 years, and ~7% away from a record high, with US AI CapEx running at over $1 trillion per year.
Meanwhile, AI-associated sectors and tech investments have accounted for ~44% of total US GDP growth on a rolling four-quarter basis.
And, Nvidia, $NVDA, is guiding nearly $750 billion in revenue for next year, even without Jensen Huang.
The underlying fundamentals of the AI Revolution have not suddenly deteriorated because of a leadership crisis at one company.
The unfortunate result of this drawdown, as with nearly every other correction since the AI Revolution began, will be countless investors getting crushed on the way back up.
Today's fearmongers become tomorrow's short squeeze as soon as sentiment shifts again.
The comments on this post will be a perfect example of just how polarized sentiment has become in the "doom" direction.
Asset owners will win and the AI Revolution is far from over.
item.content:encoded:
Take a look at sentiment right now.

Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the "AI bubble has popped."

Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression.

In reality? The S&P 500 is up +7% YTD, +60% in 5 years, and ~7% away from a record high, with US AI CapEx running at over $1 trillion per year.

Meanwhile, AI-associated sectors and tech investments have accounted for ~44% of total US GDP growth on a rolling four-quarter basis.

And, Nvidia, $NVDA, is guiding nearly $750 billion in revenue for next year, even without Jensen Huang.

The underlying fundamentals of the AI Revolution have not suddenly deteriorated because of a leadership crisis at one company.

The unfortunate result of this drawdown, as with nearly every other correction since the AI Revolution began, will be countless investors getting crushed on the way back up.

Today's fearmongers become tomorrow's short squeeze as soon as sentiment shifts again.

The comments on this post will be a perfect example of just how polarized sentiment has become in the "doom" direction.

Asset owners will win and the AI Revolution is far from over.

item.title: @wallstengine: CodeRabbit just launched Verify in public beta, an AI QA agent that tests whether code changes actu...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CodeRabbit just launched Verify in public beta, an AI QA agent that tests whether code changes actually work in a running application.
It analyzes pull requests, generates test scenarios, and runs user journeys in a browser to check whether the application behaves as intended.
When it finds a bug, it captures screenshots, session recordings, and logs so developers can see exactly what went wrong.
Here's an example from the demo:
A customer applies a SAVE20 coupon to a $100 order. The checkout correctly displays an $80 total, but the simulated charge still shows $100.
CodeRabbit Verify catches the discrepancy and provides the evidence needed to reproduce it.
Developers can then send those findings directly to CodeRabbit Agent or their preferred coding agent to implement a fix.
Testing is free during the public beta

item.title: @wallstengine: Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI s...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI services, primarily for access to OpenAI models.
The potential deal is creating tensions with OpenAI, which has raised concerns that Chinese companies could use its models to train competing AI through distillation.
Microsoft says it has found no evidence that ByteDance is doing so and believes the company primarily uses the models for software development.
ByteDance was already on track to spend roughly $1B annually on Microsoft's AI and cloud services as of June, excluding this potential deal.
While OpenAI restricts direct access for most Chinese companies, Microsoft's licensing rights allow it to sell OpenAI models through Azure to Chinese customers.
Source: The Information
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI services, primarily for access to OpenAI models.

The potential deal is creating tensions with OpenAI, which has raised concerns that Chinese companies could use its models to train competing AI through distillation.

Microsoft says it has found no evidence that ByteDance is doing so and believes the company primarily uses the models for software development.

ByteDance was already on track to spend roughly $1B annually on Microsoft's AI and cloud services as of June, excluding this potential deal.

While OpenAI restricts direct access for most Chinese companies, Microsoft's licensing rights allow it to sell OpenAI models through Azure to Chinese customers.

Source: The Information
